address: Yamatoya Bldg 9F, 1-13-7 Nishishinjuku, Shinjuku City, Tokyo
dish: Farm-to-bar cocktails from Kayama's Saitama farm; fennel-flower Sazerac, cypress-scented Martini, house absinthe (Punch)
w: Hiroyasu Kayama's apothecary-style bar with no printed menu — cocktails built from herbs and botanicals, many grown on his family farm in Saitama. World's 50 Best Bars 2025 No 18 and Asia's 50 Best No 9.

n: Virtù, Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Otemachi
address: Four Seasons Hotel Tokyo at Otemachi, 1-2-1 Otemachi, Chiyoda City, Tokyo 100-0004 (hotel address per Google Hotels; bar floor not confirmed)
dish: Virtù Martini (Japanese gin & vodka, French vermouth, hinoki bitters); thé Hoji Épicé; Takara (Japanese whisky, vermouth, Chartreuse, Denki Bran) — Time Out hotel bars
w: Art-deco cocktail bar at the Four Seasons Otemachi; the Virtù Martini uses Japanese gin and vodka with hinoki bitters. Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 No 26 and World's 50 Best Bars 2025.

address: The Tokyo EDITION, Ginza, 2-8-13 Ginza, Chuo City, Tokyo 104-0061 (mezzanine lobby) — address from Google search summary
dish: Shared punch bowls with Japanese spirits — Big Red Dot (Akadama port wine, Nikka Coffey Malt, awamori, mango, coconut tea) — Time Out
w: Punch bar inside The Tokyo EDITION, Ginza, serving shared punch bowls reworked with Japanese spirits (Big Red Dot: Akadama, Nikka Coffey Malt, awamori). Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 No 23.

address: Basement, Nishi-Ikebukuro, Toshima City, Tokyo (exact street number not found in results)
dish: Soba-tea Screwdriver twist; Fake White (gin, tomato water, Earl Grey, citrus, yoghurt wash) — 50 Best / Time Out
w: Unsigned basement bar in Nishi-Ikebukuro, a fixture for 14+ years, with inventive cocktails built on Japanese ingredients such as a soba-tea Screwdriver. Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 No 39.

address: 41-31 Udagawacho, Shibuya City, Tokyo 150-0042
dish: Yakiniku Bloody (smoked vodka, wagyu fat, yellow tomato, black garlic) — Time Out; cocktail-kaiseki course
w: Shibuya cocktail bar whose Yakiniku Bloody (smoked vodka, wagyu fat, yellow tomato, black garlic) shows its Japanese-food-inspired drinks; first entry on World's 50 Best Bars in 2025 at No 48.

address: Ginza, Chuo City, Tokyo (basement; exact address not in results)
dish: White Lady (signature); Full Bloom (maraschino + sakura liqueurs); Ueno's bespoke 'no menu' cocktails & hand-carved ice
w: Hidetsugu Ueno's Ginza basement institution with 'no menu' bespoke cocktails and hand-carved ice; regulars come for the White Lady. Long-time World's 50 Best Bars entry.

address: Dis Ebisu Bldg 102, 1-5-8 Ebisunishi, Shibuya City, Tokyo 150-0021
dish: Absinthe & herbal liqueurs; Sazerac Highball (bourbon, VSOP rouge, absinthe) — Time Out
w: Small Ebisu bar devoted to absinthe and herbal liqueurs, open since 2010; try the Sazerac Highball. Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026 extended list (No 53).

address: 8-10-15 Ginza, Chuo City, Tokyo 104-0061
dish: Aged coffee beans (old-crop beans aged 10+ years, ~50 varieties, in date-marked jars) — Time Out
w: 'Coffee only' Ginza kissaten opened in 1948 by Ichiro Sekiguchi, famous for aged coffee beans — old-crop beans kept for a decade or more in date-marked jars.

address: Shibuya, Shibuya City, Tokyo (3-min walk from Shibuya Stn; exact address not in results)
dish: Hand-drip charcoal-roasted coffee + tall chiffon cake (maple chiffon most popular) — Infatuation/Spoon & Tamago
w: Hushed, antique-filled Shibuya kissaten revered for hand-drip coffee and its tall chiffon cake; it inspired Blue Bottle's founder. Cash only.

address: Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, Koto City, Tokyo (renovated warehouse; exact address not in results)
dish: Coffee omakase / 'coffee kaiseki' tasting course — cold brew, pour-over, coffee cocktails & zero-proof drinks
w: Eiichi Kunitomo's coffee 'omakase' in a converted Kiyosumi-Shirakawa warehouse — tasting courses of pour-over, cold brew and coffee cocktails served at a counter.

address: Kayamura Bldg 1F (香村ビル１階), 3-16 Kanda Nishikicho, Chiyoda City, Tokyo 101-0054
dish: Light-roast single-origin hand drip (~15 origins); owner Kiyokazu Suzuki, 2014 Japan AeroPress champion
w: Light-roast specialty roaster in Kanda-Nishikichō pouring about 15 single origins by hand drip; owner Kiyokazu Suzuki is a former Japan AeroPress champion.

address: 1-16-11 Tomigaya, Shibuya City, Tokyo 151-0063
dish: Light-roast single-origin Nordic-style coffee by day, cocktails by night, in Scandinavian vintage interior
w: Oslo café-bar's first overseas branch (2012) in Tomigaya: light-roast Nordic coffee by day, cocktails by night, in a vintage Scandinavian interior.

address: 2-14-1 Kamimeguro, Meguro City, Tokyo (per Time Out; postcode not in result)
dish: Espresso/latte/hand drip from house-roasted beans; banana bread — Time Out; view of the Tokyu train tracks
w: Neighbourhood roastery in a small two-storey house beside the Tokyu tracks in Nakameguro — espresso and hand drip from house-roasted beans.

address: 1-2-6 Nishi-Shinjuku, Shinjuku City, Tokyo (Omoide Yokocho; per Time Out; postcode not in result)
dish: Cloth-filter hand-drip of hand-sorted house-roasted beans; coffee jelly with cream; butter toast with azuki — Time Out
w: Kissaten in Shinjuku's Omoide Yokochō since 1964: cloth-filter hand-drip coffee from hand-sorted house-roasted beans, plus coffee jelly with cream.

dish: yakitori and drinks in tiny postwar bars
n: Nonbei Yokochō, Shibuya (渋谷のんべい横丁)
address: 1-25-10 Shibuya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
w: 'Drunkard's Alley' beside the Shibuya tracks: a 1950s-era yokochō of around 39 tiny bars and eateries, some seating only four or five, dominated by yakitori shops.

dish: yakitori stalls and hole-in-the-wall bars
n: Harmonica Yokochō, Kichijōji (ハモニカ横丁)
address: Kichijōji Honchō 1-chōme (north exit of Kichijōji Station), Musashino, Tokyo
w: Postwar black-market warren of covered lanes north of Kichijōji Station, named for its harmonica-reed rows of tiny shops; by night some 56 hole-in-the-wall bars and yakitori counters under red lanterns.

dish: gyū-suji nikomi (beef stew) with Hoppy
n: Hoppy Street, Asakusa (ホッピー通り)
address: 2-5 Asakusa, Taitō-ku, Tokyo
w: An ~80 m strip of old-school open-air izakaya west of Sensō-ji, nicknamed 'Stew Street' for its bowls of beef nikomi, many still pouring Hoppy, the postwar beer-substitute mixed with shochu.

dish: Japanese craft beer on 70+ taps plus hand-pumped real ale
n: Beer Club Popeye, Ryōgoku (麦酒倶楽部ポパイ)
address: 2-18-7 Ryōgoku, Sumida-ku, Tokyo
w: Tatsuo Aoki's pioneering Ryōgoku beer bar, long regarded as Tokyo's essential craft-beer pilgrimage: 70+ taps kept in impeccable condition, mostly from Japanese breweries, plus real ales on hand pump and its own small brewery.

dish: Ushitora Brewery house IPAs and stouts among 35 taps
n: Beer Bar Ushitora, Shimokitazawa (うしとら)
address: 6-3-27 Daita, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo (Tokyo Cheapo; Time Out lists 2F, 2-9-3 Kitazawa — confirm)
w: Shimokitazawa's 'high temple of craft beer' and Tokyo taproom of Tochigi's Ushitora Brewery: 35 taps, at least seven of them house brews, with izakaya-style snacks.

dish: boutique sake flights paired with small plates (ham cutlet with blue cheese)
n: Gem by Moto, Ebisu (ジェムバイモト)
address: 1-30-9 Ebisu, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
w: Marie Chiba's counter-only Ebisu sake specialist pouring boutique sake from across Japan with seasonal small plates designed to match; reservations recommended.

dish: premium daiginjō sake with kitsune raclette (fried tofu stuffed with raclette)
address: 3-31-5 Yushima, Bunkyō-ku, Tokyo
w: Classic izakaya in business since 1925, with a long cedar counter, a master in happi coat and headband, and serious sake from a family in the sake trade for generations; house speciality kitsune raclette. Selected for Tabelog's Izakaya Hyakumeiten (EAST) 2024 and 2025.

dish: nihonshu from glass fridges behind the counter, sommelier-picked
address: 1-32-15 Uehara, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo 〒151-0064
w: Long-running Yoyogi-Uehara izakaya overseen by an English-speaking sake sommelier, with a well-chosen nihonshu list kept in glass fridges behind the counter and English drink menus.

dish: yakitori and cold beer under the brick railway arches
n: Yūrakuchō Gādo-shita, under the tracks (有楽町ガード下)
address: Brick arches under the JR Yamanote Line either side of Yūrakuchō Station, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
w: Salaryman drinking strip built into the brick arches beneath the Yamanote Line ('gādo-shita', below the girder), running nearly 700 m either side of Yūrakuchō Station: yakitori joints and izakaya with trains rumbling overhead.

dish: chūka soba (Ogikubo-style shōyu ramen); wantanmen
n: Harukiya Ogikubo Honten (春木屋 荻窪本店)
address: Kamiogi, Suginami-ku, Tokyo (Ōme-kaidō, north side of Ogikubo Station) — street number not confirmed
w: Opened 1949 and the standard-bearer of Ogikubo/Tokyo-style ramen: chūka soba blending chicken and fish stock with soy sauce, plus wantanmen and tsukemen, noodles made fresh each morning (Time Out). Ramen Adventures praises the wantanmen's broth.

dish: tsukemen (thick chicken-and-fish double-soup dipping ramen)
n: Fuunji Shinjuku Honten (風雲児 新宿本店)
address: Hokuto Dai-ichi Bldg. 1F, 2-14-3 Yoyogi, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo
w: Time Out calls it the place to go for tsukemen near Shinjuku: a thick, creamy chicken-and-fish double soup with straight noodles and queues day and night. Listed in Tabelog's Ramen Hyakumeiten TOKYO 2025.

dish: freshly kneaded udon in kombu-and-niboshi dashi
address: Koenjiminami, Suginami-ku, Tokyo — street number not confirmed
w: Michelin Bib Gourmand udon house in Kōenji: freshly kneaded, freshly boiled udon from domestic wheat in a kombu-and-dried-sardine sauce, with à la carte dishes in the evening.

dish: gyokai-tonkotsu tsukemen (also a lobster-bisque tsukemen)
address: 1-4-17 Higashishinkoiwa, Katsushika-ku, Tokyo 〒124-0023
w: Shin-Koiwa shop that Time Out and The Infatuation name among Tokyo's best tsukemen: a rich dried-fish, pork-bone and chicken soup with chāshū and tsukune toppings. A Tabelog Ramen Hyakumeiten TOKYO 2025 selection.

dish: abura soba (soupless ramen with sauce, chili oil and vinegar)
address: 5-17-21 Sakai, Musashino-shi, Tokyo
w: Hailed as the ancestor of abura soba and serving the same menu since 1965 near Musashi-Sakai Station: medium-thick noodles over a meaty sauce, topped with menma, chāshū and naruto, dressed with house chili oil and vinegar (Time Out).

dish: tsukemen
address: Kameari, Katsushika-ku, Tokyo — street number not confirmed
w: Kameari tsukemen specialist with its own Ramen Adventures listing and a place in Tokyo Cheapo's top-10 Tokyo tsukemen restaurants.

dish: dorayaki (honey-batter pancakes sandwiching aged Tokachi azuki paste)
address: 1-10-10 Ueno, Taitō-ku, Tokyo 〒110-0005
w: Century-old Ueno wagashi shop widely cited as one of Tokyo's three great dorayaki makers; the Japan Times profiled it as one of the two shops claiming to have created the dorayaki. Its dorayaki uses aged azuki paste in a honey-infused batter.

dish: taiyaki (fish-shaped cake filled with adzuki paste)
address: 1-8-14 Azabujuban, Minato-ku, Tokyo 〒106-0045
w: Opened in Azabu-Jūban in 1909 and, per the Japan Times, the shop popularly credited with originating taiyaki; also on Time Out's best-taiyaki list.

dish: yōkan (red-bean jelly) and seasonal namagashi
n: Toraya Akasaka flagship (とらや 赤坂店)
address: 4-9-22 Akasaka, Minato-ku, Tokyo 〒107-8401
w: Flagship of Toraya, the 500-year-old former Imperial Court confectioner, rebuilt in 2018 by architect Hiroshi Naito with a shop, factory, Toraya café and gallery; the signature is yōkan.

dish: Kūya monaka (caramelised wafer shells filled with house azuki paste)
address: 6-7-19 Ginza, Chūō-ku, Tokyo
w: Monaka maker founded in 1884 in Ueno Ikenohata and in Ginza since the war; its monaka appears in Natsume Sōseki's 'I Am a Cat' and must usually be reserved in advance.

dish: sakadane anpan (sake-yeast bun with bean paste and a salt-pickled sakura blossom)
address: 4-5-7 Ginza, Chūō-ku, Tokyo
w: Japan's oldest bakery, which created the anpan in 1874 using sake yeast; its sakura anpan was presented to Emperor Meiji.

dish: kakigōri (hand-cranked shaved Nikkō natural ice with fresh-fruit syrups)
address: 3-11-18 Yanaka, Taitō-ku, Tokyo
w: Yanaka kakigōri specialist shaving natural Nikkō ice on a hand-cranked machine, with natural syrups and fresh fruit; unusually it serves kakigōri year-round.

dish: jumbo melonpan
address: Asakusa, Taitō-ku, Tokyo (main shop near Sensō-ji; Kaminarimon branch also)
w: Asakusa fixture since 1945 that sells essentially one thing — a crisp-topped jumbo melonpan best eaten warm, often sold out by 4pm.

dish: Bricolage bread (ancient-grain country loaf), pistachio escargot, tropézienne
n: Bricolage Bread & Co. (ブリコラージュ ブレッド アンド カンパニー)
address: Roppongi, Minato-ku, Tokyo
w: Roppongi bakery-café from L'Effervescence chef Shinobu Namae, baker Ayumu Iwanaga and Fuglen's Kenji Kojima; signature deep-crusted Bricolage loaf from ancient grains. Selected for Tabelog Bread TOKYO Hyakumeiten 2026.
